issue: Pulumi state: bucket replacement loop. GCP returned 409 'bucket already exists' because Pulumi state had pendingReplacement:true on the bucket resource, location mismatch ('US' vs actual 'EUROPE-WEST3'), and a duplicate api-images registry URN (us-central1 and europe-west3 both in state). Pulumi tried to delete-then-recreate the bucket on every run.
fix: Exported state JSON, removed duplicate us-central1 registry entry, corrected bucket location to EUROPE-WEST3, removed pendingReplacement flag, re-imported state, ran pulumi refresh to sync. Also deleted stale us-central1 Artifact Registry repo from GCP directly.

issue: Cloud Run reserved env var. Pulumi infra/index.ts had PORT=8080 in container envs. Cloud Run injects PORT automatically and rejects any attempt to set it manually: 'Error 400: spec.template.spec.containers[0].env: The following reserved env names were provided: PORT'
fix: Removed { name: 'PORT', value: '8080' } from container envs in infra/index.ts

issue: Same PORT=8080 reserved env var in the gcloud run deploy step inside deploy.yml. The --set-env-vars string included PORT=8080.
fix: Removed PORT=8080 from --set-env-vars in deploy.yml gcloud run deploy step.

issue: Test and Infra jobs passed for first time. Deploy job built and pushed image OK, but container failed to start on Cloud Run. Cloud Run health probe timed out. Cloud Run logs showed: PathError [TypeError]: Missing parameter name at index 1: * at server.ts:67. Express 5 upgraded path-to-regexp to v8 which removed bare * wildcard support.
fix: Changed app.get('*', ...) to app.get('{*path}', ...) in packages/api/src/server.ts to use Express 5 / path-to-regexp v8 compatible syntax.

issue: None. All three jobs passed: Test (36s), Infra (46s), Deploy (1m55s). Cloud Run URL: https://bedtime-api-del75zytpq-ey.a.run.app. API responding with 401 on /api/auth/me (auth guard working correctly).
fix: No fix needed. However discovered immediately after: root URL '/' also returns 401 because app.use(requireAuth) is global middleware placed before static file serving in server.ts. Static files get auth-gated. Fix: scope requireAuth to /api only.

issue: Frontend HTML/CSS/JS unreachable in production. app.use(requireAuth) in server.ts is a global middleware that runs before the static file serving block. Any unauthenticated request to / or any asset path returns 401 before Express even reaches express.static(). The React SPA cannot load without auth, creating a chicken-and-egg problem.
fix: Changed app.use(requireAuth) to app.use('/api', requireAuth) in packages/api/src/server.ts. This scopes auth enforcement to /api/* paths only. /api/auth/* was already registered before this middleware so login endpoints remain public. Static files at /* are now served without auth, which is correct — the SPA handles its own auth state client-side.

issue: Frontend returning 404 on /. Two causes: (1) webDist path in server.ts was '../../../web/dist' resolving to /app/web/dist, but Dockerfile puts it at /app/packages/web/dist — needed '../../web/dist'. (2) GET /healthz added before requireAuth for Cloud Run health probes and deploy verification. Also: Cloud Run domain mappings unsupported in europe-west3, so adding Global HTTPS LB (static IP + serverless NEG + managed SSL cert + HTTP redirect) via Pulumi. Route53 A record upsert added to infra job.
fix: Fixed webDist path. Added /healthz route. Added full LB stack to infra/index.ts. Added post-pulumi Route53 upsert step (requires PROD_ROUTE53_ZONE_ID var + PROD_AWS_* secrets in GHA prod environment).

issue: Health check returned 404 (Google's 404 page, not our app). Root cause: Pulumi runs `pulumi up` on every push and resets the Cloud Run service template to the placeholder image `hello:latest` because `infra/index.ts` has that as the declared image. When two pushes happen in quick succession, the concurrent Pulumi run from the second push overwrites the real image deployed by the first push's `gcloud run deploy`. The health check then hits the hello:latest image which has no /healthz route. Even within a single run, every Pulumi run resets the image before `gcloud run deploy` restores it.
fix: Added ignoreChanges: ['template'] to the Cloud Run service Pulumi resource. Pulumi creates the service once with the placeholder, but never updates the template configuration again. `gcloud run deploy` in the deploy job is the sole owner of the running container config.

issue: Health check was hardcoded to use raw Cloud Run URL. User wants it to verify the custom domain (bedtime-agent.ilya.online) once DNS is set up.
fix: Changed health check to use PROD_APP_URL variable if set, falling back to gcloud-described Cloud Run URL. After DNS + cert are live, add PROD_APP_URL=https://bedtime-agent.ilya.online as a prod environment variable in GitHub.

issue: GET /healthz returns Google GFE 404 HTML and never reaches the container. Confirmed by comparing response headers: /healthz response has no x-cloud-trace-context or x-powered-by headers (meaning the request never reached Cloud Run), while /health and /readyz DO reach Express. Root cause: Knative (which Cloud Run is built on) reserves /healthz for its own internal health-check infrastructure at the GFE layer. Requests to /healthz are intercepted before the container receives them.
fix: Renamed health endpoint from /healthz to /_healthz in packages/api/src/server.ts. Updated the health check URL in .github/workflows/deploy.yml to match. The underscore prefix avoids all Knative/Cloud Run reserved path conflicts.

issue: None. All three jobs passed: Test (27s), Infra (43s), Deploy (2m3s). Health check GET /_healthz returns {"status":"ok"} 200. Cloud Run URL: https://bedtime-api-28324530789.europe-west3.run.app. Pipeline fully operational.
